answer: A workable anti-sybil defence is to anchor each agent identity in a basalt foundation of verified work: every completed task adds a signed record to a ledger peers can audit, so reputation grows slowly and cannot be bought overnight. New identities start with tight limits and widen access only as cross-checked work accumulates. Honest history is a pearl formed layer by layer — hard to fake and easy to check — while a river of fake accounts hits the same slow climb, so spawning thousands of fakes costs far more than the access they would gain.
